content: YY1, also known as Yin Yang 1, is a transcriptional repressor protein in humans encoded by the YY1 gene. This protein is a ubiquitously distributed transcription factor that belongs to the GLI-Kruppel class of zinc finger proteins. YY1 plays a dual role in gene regulation, as it can both repress and activate a wide variety of promoters. The name Yin Yang reflects this dual functionality. YY1 is capable of directing histone deacetylases (HDACs) and histone acetyltransferases (HATs) to specific promoters, thereby modulating promoter activity through histone modification. This highlights the critical role of histone modifications in the regulatory functions of YY1. Additionally, YY1 facilitates the formation of enhancer-promoter chromatin loops by forming dimers and promoting DNA interactions. Disruption of YY1 function can lead to the breakdown of these chromatin loops, resulting in altered gene expression. Clinically, heterozygous deletions, missense mutations, and nonsense mutations in the YY1 gene are associated with Gabriele-De Vries syndrome (GADEVS). This is an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, feeding difficulties, intrauterine growth restriction, variable cognitive impairment, behavioral problems, and other congenital malformations. A dedicated website exists to facilitate the sharing and collection of clinical information among healthcare providers and families of individuals with YY1 mutations. YY1 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including: Activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), EP300 (a histone acetyltransferase), FKBP3 (FK506-binding protein 3), HDAC3 (histone deacetylase 3), Histone deacetylase 2, MYC (a proto-oncogene), NOTCH1 (a transmembrane receptor involved in cell signaling), RYBP (Ring1 and YY1 binding protein), SAP30 (Sin3-associated protein 30), and Seryl-tRNA synthetase. These interactions underscore the multifaceted role of YY1 in cellular processes and gene regulation.
